items.title: Why are international agencies exposing corruption Ghana cannot detect? — MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, has questioned why Ghana’s domestic security and anti-corruption institutions often fail to uncover alleged corruption schemes that are subsequently exposed by foreign law enforcement agencies. He said the conviction of former Goldman Sachs banker Asante Kwaku Berko in the United States should prompt Ghana to examine not only the alleged bribery of Ghanaian officials but also weaknesses within institutions responsible for detecting and investigating corruption. Speaking on Joy FM’s News Night on Thursday, August 13, 2026, the NPP MP said the Berko case was not an isolated incident and argued that Ghana could not afford to allow such cases to go without a comprehensive investigation. “We are dealing with a gentleman that has been convicted in the United States of America for paying bribes to persons in authority. This is not the first time this is happening in the Republic of Ghana. It has happened over and over again,” he said. His comments come after a federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, convicted Mr Berko on August 6, 2026, over his role in a scheme involving the payment of more than US$1 million in bribes to Ghanaian officials in connection with the development and financing of a power plant. Mr Berko, a dual Ghanaian-American citizen and former executive director in the investment banking division of Goldman Sachs, had been involved in securing and managing an agreement between the Ghanaian government and Turkish energy company Aksa Enerji Uretim A.S. According to the US prosecution, the scheme involved discussions about payments to Ghanaian officials to facilitate approvals for the project. The US Department of Justice also said Ghanaian officials received payments during a trip to Turkey to inspect equipment for the proposed power plant. The conviction has since triggered calls for investigations in Ghana to establish whether officials allegedly involved in the scheme received bribes and whether any wrongdoing occurred on the Ghanaian side. For Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, however, the matter goes beyond identifying individuals who may have benefited from the alleged scheme. “The fundamental question that we have to answer, all of us, is, why is it that domestic security agencies keep missing this point, but international agencies are the ones that are getting this exposed?” he asked. He said Ghana needed to use the case to assess the effectiveness of its institutions and determine why allegations of corruption involving public officials were sometimes detected outside the country rather than by domestic agencies. “Are we saying that we should leave it and let it go without dealing with it so that Ghana will be continuously embarrassed on the international plane?” he asked. Call for public inquiry The MP advocated a public inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the power project and the alleged bribery scheme, saying such an exercise should not be viewed as an initiative designed to benefit the political opposition. He also questioned whether the Minority had information on the identity of an alleged relative of then-President John Mahama who has been referenced in discussions surrounding the case. “My question to you is, does the minority have any idea who the cited relative of then President John Mahama could be? We are asking for the inquiry. It is not something which should be to the benefit of merely the minority but the whole of Ghana,” he said. Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah said a public inquiry would provide an opportunity to examine the conduct of state institutions and identify systemic weaknesses that could allow corruption to go undetected. “How do we get it done? It is through a public inquiry,” he said. He added: “Because you see, it is not merely to have people punished. It is also to look at our institutions, institutions of state, and how they do not, how they are not able to, you know, deal with or discover these matters.” The MP said the Berko case should therefore be treated as an opportunity to strengthen Ghana’s institutional mechanisms for detecting corruption rather than simply focusing on possible criminal liability. “But they are only discovered by international bodies,” he said, stressing the need for Ghana to examine why foreign investigations were able to uncover the alleged scheme. The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has disclosed that it provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in the Berko case through Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework. The OSP said the US Department of Justice acknowledged its assistance as having made a “significant” contribution to the prosecution. The Attorney-General and Minister of Justice has also indicated that Ghanaian authorities will work with US counterparts to investigate the Ghanaian side of the case. Mr Berko is scheduled to be sentenced by the US court on November 10, 2026.

items.title: Modernisation du système éducatif: L’École sénégalaise à l’ère numérique
items.description: Le système éducatif sénégalais doit accélérer sa transformation numérique pour permettre aux autorités de disposer de données fiables et exploitables en temps réel, a plaidé jeudi le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Moustapha Mamba Guirassy. À l’ouverture de l’atelier national stratégique d’appropriation et de déploiement de l’écosystème numérique éducatif, il a relevé l’existence de plusieurs plateformes performantes, notamment dans les statistiques et la gestion des ressources humaines, mais encore insuffisamment intégrées. Le ministre a appelé à « développer une intelligence de ces plateformes », à les unifier et à privilégier des solutions pragmatiques. Il a notamment cité le Système national d’évaluation des rendements scolaires (Sners), dont les résultats peuvent parvenir aux autorités plusieurs années après la collecte des données. « Lorsque je les reçois, c’est déjà trop tard », a-t-il déploré, estimant que les moyens humains, financiers et administratifs consacrés aux évaluations perdent une partie de leur portée lorsque leurs résultats ne permettent pas d’éclairer la décision à temps. Moustapha Mamba Guirassy veut ainsi faire du numérique un outil de pilotage « dans l’instantanéité », permettant de suivre l’évolution du système éducatif à tout moment. Cette ambition s’appuie notamment sur le déploiement de Planète 3 et la dématérialisation progressive des inscriptions et réinscriptions scolaires. Le ministère a par ailleurs engagé une refonte de son système d’information pour passer « d’applications fonctionnant en silos à un écosystème numérique intégré, interopérable, sécurisé et orienté vers les usages ». Cette intégration doit favoriser une meilleure articulation des données, plateformes et services numériques, tout en renforçant les outils d’aide à la décision et l’accès aux services pour les établissements, les enseignants et les familles. Au terme des trois jours de travaux, le ministre souhaite des « solutions concrètes et opérationnelles » susceptibles de « complètement changer le visage de l’École », en faisant du numérique un levier de pilotage, d’efficacité et d’amélioration des apprentissages.

items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs0.45, high-speed diesel by Rs1.16
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.16. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325.43 per litre while HSD will cost Rs383.95 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 14 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Sissili/JIJ 2026 : La jeunesse de la Sissili appelée à s’approprier le développement et à se mobiliser pour la souveraineté nationale et confédérale
items.description: Sissili/JIJ 2026 : La jeunesse de la Sissili appelée à s’approprier le développement et à se mobiliser pour la souveraineté nationale et confédérale Léo, 12 août 2026 (AIB) – La province de la Sissili a célébré, ce mercredi 12 août 2026 à Léo, la Journée internationale de la jeunesse (JIJ). Placée sous la présidence du haut-commissaire de la province, Téwindé Isaac Sia, cette journée a été marquée par une marche à travers les grandes artères de la ville, des hommages aux figures historiques locales, des panels de réflexion et des activités sportives, le tout axé sur l’engagement patriotique et la souveraineté. C’est par une marche de soutien à la RPP à travers les grandes artères du centre-ville de Léo que les forces vives de la province ont lancé les activités de la Journée internationale de la jeunesse, placée cette année sous le thème « Rôle, responsabilité et engagement de la jeunesse burkinabè dans la construction d’un espace confédéral souverain ». Livrant le message officiel de la ministre de la Jeunesse, des Sports et de l’Emploi, camarade Annick Lydie Djouma Pikbougoum/Zingué Ouattara, le premier responsable de la province a transmis les hommages de la Nation à la jeunesse burkinabè, des villes comme des campagnes, y compris les élèves, étudiants, travailleurs et Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP). À travers ce message, l’exécutif a salué la résilience et l’engagement constant de la jeunesse depuis les luttes historiques jusqu’à l’avènement de la Révolution progressiste et populaire (RPP). Le gouvernement a rappelé la mise en place du Plan RELANCE 2026-2030 et de l’initiative « Jeunesse Révolutionnaire en Marche » (JeRM), tout en invitant les jeunes à porter les valeurs de l’espace confédéral et à lutter contre la lâcheté, la traîtrise et l’incompétence. Pour le haut-commissaire Téwindé Isaac Sia, cette célébration invite la jeunesse à s’investir concrètement dans le développement local. Il a exhorté les jeunes à « s’organiser activement autour des actions communautaires », citant notamment la réparation des routes et la gestion des infrastructures. L’objectif étant, selon lui, « que ces initiatives soient prises en main directement par les jeunes » afin de faire barrière aux manœuvres de déstabilisation. Dans le même esprit, le directeur provincial du Sport, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, Denis Nikièma, s’est félicité de la forte mobilisation des forces vives. Soulignant qu’il faut cesser de « tout attendre de nos parents », Camarade Nikièma a affirmé que « le développement appartient à la jeunesse » qui doit prendre des initiatives sans attendre l’extérieur, tout en plaidant pour la mise en place de mécanismes de financement adaptés pour les porteurs de projets. Prenant la parole au nom de la tradition, Sa Majesté Lio-Pio Dan-Zwè, Chef de Canton de Léo, a rappelé le rôle protecteur dévolu aux jeunes en période de crise : « Lorsque la patrie risque de s’échapper, c’est à la jeunesse de courir pour la rattraper », a-t-il affirmé. Insistant sur la valeur du travail et de l’autonomie financière, le souverain coutumier a rappelé qu’« une jeunesse autonome est une jeunesse qu’on ne peut plus corrompre », avant d’appeler les jeunes à se mettre au travail « à la sueur de leur front ». Sa Majesté a conclu en formulant des bénédictions pour la jeunesse et pour le président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Au-delà des allocutions, la journée a été marquée par un hommage solennel aux figures historiques de la Sissili, notamment Bamina Georges Nébié, premier ministre de la Défense de Haute-Volta, et les anciens CDR Lady Ziba et Mamouna Yago. L’ancien CDR Ladji Saïdou Nébié a également été présenté et ovationné par le public. Les participants ont ensuite pris part à des panels consacrés à la vie du Capitaine Thomas Sankara et aux similitudes entre la Révolution démocratique et populaire (RDP) et la RPP impulsée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Les manifestations se sont achevées dans une ambiance conviviale par une séance d’aérobic sur le plateau de la Maison des Jeunes de Léo. Agence d’Information du Burkina BAN/ata

items.title: NEITI audit queries pit Finance Ministry against NNPCL
items.description: — As $3bn pre-export loan, $722.6m LNG dividends, others remain unresolved By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Federal Ministry of Finance and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPCL, on Thursday traded blame over unresolved queries raised in the 2021–2023 Oil and Gas Sector Audit Report by the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative, NEITI. The development followed the appearance of the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance, Mr Raymond Omachi, before the Senate Committee on Public Accounts, chaired by Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo (PDP, Gombe North), to respond to financial queries contained in the NEITI report. Omachi told the committee that the ministry was unable to provide some of the records required to address the queries because agencies involved in the transactions, particularly the NNPCL, had not made the necessary financial documents available. One of the issues raised by NEITI relates to a $3 billion pre-export financing loan obtained in 2012 to settle subsidy payments. According to the audit report, the recovery of the loan from monthly Federation revenue proceeds under the Pre-Export Financing and Project Eagle agreements remained unclear. Another query concerns $722.6 million paid by the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, to the then Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, NNPC, in 2021 as dividends and interest earned on behalf of the Federation. NEITI said the money was neither remitted to the Federation nor properly accounted for. The committee also considered the audit finding that none of Nigeria’s refineries was operational in 2021 despite about N200 billion reportedly spent on them. Another unresolved issue was the $221.283 million in overhead costs incurred by the National Petroleum Investment Management Services, NAPIMS, in 2021. Responding to the queries, Omachi said the Ministry of Finance was not directly involved in all the transactions under review, making it dependent on the relevant agencies for supporting documents. He said: “We don’t have direct involvement in all the issues raised and required provision of financial records from the affected agencies, particularly NNPCL, NUPRC, etc., is not there.” The Permanent Secretary disclosed that the ministry had engaged external auditors, Arthur Andersen LLP, to conduct a forensic audit of the transactions and reconcile the records. However, Dankwambo questioned the ministry on when the forensic audit report would be ready, noting that the exercise had already been extended twice, from six months to one year. The committee chairman also insisted that the NNPCL and the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NUPRC, should appear alongside the Ministry of Finance at a subsequent sitting to provide explanations on the outstanding issues. Dankwambo said the ministry had the authority to ensure that the affected agencies appeared before the committee. “I know you have enormous powers that you can use to compel these agencies to appear before us. We are having challenges bringing them to the table so that we can resolve these issues,” he said. He added: “We in the Federal Ministry of Finance are ready to come and sit with them here, so that you can hear directly from them and obtain the necessary explanations and clarifications.” The committee chairman directed the Permanent Secretary to review the ministry’s internal report and arrange a joint meeting involving the Ministry of Finance, NUPRC, NNPCL and any other relevant agency. Dankwambo said the issues required urgent resolution because they were being monitored beyond Nigeria. “I will like you to review the internal report and arrange a meeting involving the Ministry of Finance, the NUPRC, NNPC and any other agency whose participation is necessary to resolve the issues we have raised,” he said. “As you are aware, these issues are being followed by the international community. They are not matters confined to Nigeria; they are in the public domain and are being monitored by people across the world. “Therefore, if there are records or issues that need to be clarified and properly put in order, we should do so in the interest of our country. All of us have no other country except Nigeria.” The committee is expected to continue its review of the audit queries after the relevant agencies provide the requested records and explanations. items.title: Osun Election: Bola Oyebamiji – strengths, weaknesses
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO With less than two days to the governorship election in Osun State and the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, confirming that 2,339, 233 residents registered to participate in the polls, candidates and political parties are rounding up campaign and intensifying moves to warm themselves into the hearts of the people with a view to winning their support to emerge as the next Governor of the state. Out of the 15 candidates, only three have presented manifestoes and commenced campaigns. Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress, APC, is one of them. Strengths The APC candidate is believed to enjoy the support of President Bola Tinubu and the APC governors, who will stop at nothing to ensure victory for the party at the polls. The APC candidate’s personality and philanthropy has endeared him to the people. Apart from being endorsed by the President, Oyebamiji’s election bid receive a major boost with the defection of all the federal lawmakers from Osun-East senatorial district, who are also major political gladiators from the towns. They include Senator Francis Fadahunsi, Mr Wole Oke (Ijesa-North federal constituency), Sanya Omirin (Ijesa-South federal constituency) and Mr Taofeek Ajilesoro (Ife federal constituency). The defectors are seen as turning the tide in favour of the APC candidate in their respective strongholds. Their action, according to party leaders, may tilt the pendulum in favour of Oyebamiji from the senatorial district. Besides, some of Omisore’s point men in Ife have also pledged loyalty to the party and its candidate. While Adeleke got massive votes from Osun-West in 2022, the candidature of Oyebamiji may change the narrative, with the total registered votes from Ikire federal constituency amounting to 222,786 votes for Irewole, Ayedaade and Isokan local governments, likely reducing the influence of the governor in the district. While Governor Adeleke seems to enjoy endorsement among royal fathers from Ife, Oyebamiji’s major endorsement programme has been coming from markets and traders. In most of his engagements, the APC candidate has always taken advantage of the allegation of nepotism against the incumbent to sell himself as a man for all. Although the APC has not started its campaign, the party has completed the inauguration of 30 vote canvassers for each of the 3,763 polling units across the state. Oyebamiji is likely to win in Osun-East due to the presence of Senator Francis Fadahunsi, a major political gladiator from Ijesaland, Hon Sanya Omirin and Hon Wole Oke from Ijesa-South and North respectively. Although, Senator Iyiola Omisore is still a member of the APC, some of his loyalists are still within the party. Also Engr. Kayode Adereti, the deputy governorship candidate of he party, is influencial having contested against incumbent member of the House of Representatives in 2022 – Taofeek Ajilesoro, who is now also in the APC. In Osun-Central, whoever wins in Osogbo and Olorunda local government is likely to win the senatorial district. Oyebamiji has the likes of the party’s national secretary, Senator Ajibola Basiru who is from the core Osogbo supported by Executive Director, Marine and Blue Economy, Olalekan Badmus and many elites in the Olorunda and Osogbo, supporting the APC. Challenges Oyebamiji’s major issue is the policy decision of the Oyetola administration under whom he served. The modulated salary under Governor Rauf Aregbesola and the inability of Governor Gboyega Oyetola to pay part of it has been a major issue confronting his candidature. His critics, especially from the Accord party, believe he is responsible for the modulated salary under Aregbesola’s administration and should not be trusted with the governorship seat. items.title: DTI graduates over 1,500 master crafts persons, SMES to drive formalisation of Ghana’s informal sector
items.description: More than 1,500 Master Craft Persons (MCPs) and Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) owners have graduated from the Design and Technology Institute’s (DTI) Precision Quality (PQ) training programme, in a move aimed at accelerating the formalisation and competitiveness of Ghana’s informal sector. The graduation ceremony, held at the National Theatre in Accra, brought together government officials, development partners, industry stakeholders, financial institutions and the graduates to celebrate the achievements of artisans and entrepreneurs who successfully completed the competency-based training programme. The initiative forms part of DTI’s partnership with the Mastercard Foundation to equip informal businesses with technical, business and management skills. Speaking to JoyBusiness on the sidelines of the event, Founder and President of DTI, Constance Elizabeth Swaniker, said the programme is transforming Ghana’s informal sector by helping artisans improve the quality of their products, strengthen their businesses and create more opportunities for young apprentices. She noted that the training goes beyond technical skills by equipping participants with knowledge in business management, workplace safety, customer service, financial management and digital tools, making them better positioned to compete in both local and international markets. According to her, formalising the informal sector is critical to Ghana’s industrial transformation because the country’s informal apprenticeship system remains the largest source of skills development. She stressed that empowering master craftspeople with internationally recognised standards ultimately improves employment opportunities for young people while raising productivity across the sector. The PQ programme is aligned with Ghana’s Human Capital Development Strategy, which seeks to formalise the country’s apprenticeship system through structured training, certification and enterprise support. Under the programme, participating master craftspeople are required to engage apprentices or young employees, ensuring skills are transferred to the next generation while expanding employment opportunities. Some of the graduands who spoke to JoyBusiness described the training as a turning point for their businesses. They said the programme had strengthened their technical competencies while improving their understanding of bookkeeping, customer relations, business planning and quality assurance. They expressed confidence that the certification would enhance the credibility of their businesses and enable them to attract more customers and expand their operations. The graduates also welcomed the emphasis on business formalisation, saying it would help them access financing, register their businesses and take advantage of new market opportunities. This year’s Accra graduation certified 1,583 Master Craft Persons and SME owners, with similar ceremonies expected to be held in Ho and Kumasi as DTI continues to expand the programme nationwide. The graduation programme also included testimonies from beneficiaries, discussions on financial inclusion, business registration and the creation of an MCP Alumni Association to provide continued support and networking opportunities for graduates.

items.title: Catholic priests reject FG’s ranching plan for Benue
items.description: …warn against land grabbing By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Nigeria Catholic Diocesan Priests Association, NCDPA, Makurdi Diocese, has rejected the Federal Government’s decision to include Benue State in the pilot implementation of its National Ranching Policy, warning that the plan could threaten ancestral lands and the security of residents. The Minister of Livestock Development, Alhaji Idi Maiha, had disclosed that the Federal Government identified five states, including Benue and the Federal Capital Territory, for the pilot implementation of the National Ranching Policy. Reacting to the development, the NCDPA, in a statement signed by its Chairman, Rev. Fr. Joseph Beba, described Benue as an “already bleeding and targeted state,” while expressing concern over the alleged exclusion of the state government from the decision-making process. The priests said: “Had the elected leadership of Benue State been genuinely consulted, we believe it would never have consented to any arrangement capable of undermining the rights, dignity, security and ancestral heritage of our people.” The association said it could not accept what it described as the imposition of a policy on communities that had suffered killings, displacement, destruction and prolonged insecurity. It warned that ranching must not become “a disguised instrument for land grabbing, forced occupation or the permanent displacement of indigenous communities.” The priests also commended the Catholic Bishop of Makurdi Diocese, Bishop Wilfred Anagbe, for what they described as his consistent opposition to injustice and policies they believe could threaten the ancestral lands of Benue people. “There is no going back on this as long as we still draw breath,” the statement declared. The NCDPA called on the Federal Government to respect the constitutional rights of Benue residents and engage the state government, traditional rulers and community leaders transparently before implementing any ranching arrangement in the state. It also demanded the safe return of Internally Displaced Persons, IDPs, to their communities and the restoration of their access to their ancestral lands. The association maintained that Benue remained predominantly an agrarian state and argued that commercial ranching was not viable in the state. “Ranching in Benue State is therefore not viable, and we reject this project idea with all legal and spiritual resources,” it said. The priests declared that “our land is not for sale and has never been on sale,” insisting that there was no land in Benue available for commercial ranching. “Our ancestral homes are not bargaining chips. Our people must return home. Benue must not be enslaved through policy,” the statement added. The NCDPA urged the Federal Government to reconsider the plan and adopt policies that would guarantee the safety, dignity and land rights of residents, while facilitating the return of displaced communities to their ancestral homes. items.title: Sissili/Gouvernance : La délégation spéciale de la commune urbaine de Léo tient sa première session extraordinaire de l’année 2026
items.description: Sissili/Gouvernance : La délégation spéciale de la commune urbaine de Léo tient sa première session extraordinaire de l’année 2026 Léo, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – La Délégation spéciale de la commune de Léo a tenu, le mercredi 12 août 2026 dans la salle des fêtes de la mairie, sa première session extraordinaire. Présidée par Kassoum Koalaga, Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS), cette rencontre s’est penchée sur plusieurs délibérations touchant au recrutement du personnel, à la fiscalité locale, à l’aménagement urbain et à l’assainissement. Pendant cette session extraordinaire réunissant l’ensemble des 18 délégués de la commune, les membres de la délégation spéciale ont examiné et adopté un ordre du jour particulièrement chargé, axé sur les préoccupations majeures des populations locales. Au titre des affaires administratives et du renforcement des ressources humaines, les délégués ont délibéré sur l’autorisation d’ouverture de deux concours professionnels. Il s’agit du recrutement d’un élève adjoint administratif et d’un élève assistant des services financiers au titre de l’année 2026. Pour mener à bien ces opérations, la délégation a approuvé la signature d’une convention cadre avec l’Agence nationale d’appui au développement des collectivités territoriales (ADCT). Sur le plan foncier et domanial, deux importantes délibérations ont porté sur l’institution de droits de timbres communaux, s’appliquant désormais aux actes de construire ainsi qu’aux attestations de possession foncière rurale (APFR) délivrés par la mairie. De plus, la session a donné un avis favorable au changement de destination de deux parcelles à usage initial d’habitation vers un usage commercial. À l’ouverture des travaux, le PDS de Léo, Kassoum Koalaga, a tenu à saluer la mobilisation et l’engagement constant des délégués. Il a également justifié le réaménagement de l’horaire initial de la session en raison des activités commémoratives de la Journée internationale de la jeunesse. « La tenue de cette session répond à la nécessité d’examiner avec diligence les questions inscrites à notre ordre du jour et de prendre, dans le respect des textes en vigueur, les décisions nécessaires à la bonne marche de notre municipalité », a affirmé Kassoum Koalaga. Le président de la délégation spéciale a invité l’assemblée à un esprit de rigueur et de cohésion pour l’intérêt général. « Nos décisions doivent s’inscrire dans la dynamique de développement de la commune de Léo et contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie de nos concitoyens» a souligné le PDS Koalaga. Rendant compte des retombées de ces échanges, Bakora Ernest Bassolé, membre de la délégation spéciale, s’est réjoui de la portée pratique des délibérations adoptées. « Cette session extraordinaire a porté sur des sujets d’intérêt général au bénéfice de la population. Il est essentiel que les citoyens soient informés des décisions prises à la mairie », a déclaré Ernest Bassolé. Revenant sur les recrutements et les réaménagements fonciers, il a souligné que le renforcement des effectifs permettra de répondre à une forte demande de services publics. S’agissant du changement de destination des parcelles, M. Bassolé a précisé que ces espaces permettront notamment l’aménagement d’auberges destinées à offrir un hébergement sécurisé aux visiteurs et missionnaires de passage à Léo. Abordant le point des divers, axé principalement sur l’assainissement de la ville et la dégradation des voies, camarade Bassolé a lancé un appel au civisme des administrés « Les citoyens doivent adhérer à ces initiatives et nous accompagner. Il ne faut pas toujours attendre l’intervention de la mairie ou de la Délégation Spéciale pour maintenir notre cadre de vie propre » a-t-il exhorté. Agence d’Information du Burkina BAN/ata

items.title: We don’t have confidence in AG to independently probe AKSA energy deal – NPP
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it has no confidence in the Attorney General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, to independently investigate or prosecute persons implicated in the latest bribery allegations surrounding the AKSA Energy power project. The party argues that the investigation must be conducted in a manner that inspires public confidence, particularly because some of the persons who could come under scrutiny are allegedly politically connected to the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). Speaking at a press briefing at the NPP headquarters in Accra on Thursday, August 13, the party’s Manhyia South MP, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, cited several cases in which the Attorney General has discontinued or abandoned prosecutions involving persons linked to previous or current administrations. “The NPP wishes to place on record its lack of confidence in the current Attorney General as far as the handling of this matter is concerned,” he said. He accused Dr Ayine of being associated with the discontinuation or non-prosecution of cases since assuming office in January 2025. Mr Awuah cited the SSNIT scandal, Saglemi Housing Project case, Cocobod-related cases and the Unibank case among matters in which the Attorney General has entered a nolle prosequi. He said the decisions had raised questions about accountability, transparency and the recovery of public funds. The NPP MP also singled out the Unibank case, which he said formed part of the wider banking sector clean-up and involved significant public expenditure. He criticised the Attorney General over what he described as a failure to disclose key information to Parliament and to make public details of a proposed plea bargain involving the accused persons. “Against this background, we do not believe that the Attorney General can command the confidence of the Ghanaian public to independently investigate or prosecute allegations involving officials or politically connected persons of the NDC,” he said. Mr Awuah argued that the repeated discontinuation of prosecutions involving persons associated with the NDC administration had created a perception of selective accountability. He said the NPP was therefore calling for an investigation based on evidence rather than political affiliation. The NPP is also demanding clarification about the identity and alleged role of a person described in US court proceedings as a relative of then-President John Mahama in connection with the AKSA deal. Mr Awuah said investigators must establish the person’s identity, relationship with President Mahama, involvement in the transaction and whether the individual received any money. “The Ghanaian public deserves to know who this person was. What was the person’s relationship with President John Dramani Mahama? What company or entity was the person associated with? What role did the person play in the AKSA transaction?” he asked. He further demanded answers on whether the individual received money and, if so, how much and for what purpose. The Manhyia South MP said the issue raised concerns similar to those surrounding the Airbus controversy, where a person described in court records as a close relative of a high-ranking Ghanaian official featured in the case. He said the investigation must also establish whether the alleged relative’s involvement influenced the approval process for the AKSA project. The NPP’s demands come amid renewed scrutiny of the AKSA Energy power project following the conviction in the United States of former Goldman Sachs banker and former Tema Oil Refinery Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko in a bribery and money-laundering case linked to the project.

items.title: Police officer killed as suspected herders attack Benue checkpoint
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A police officer has been killed in an attack on a joint police and military checkpoint in Uzer community, Logo Local Government Area of Benue State. The incident, reportedly carried out by suspected armed herders, occurred when the attackers stormed the security checkpoint, prompting troops of Sector 1, Operation Whirl Stroke, stationed in Ayilamo, and a team of mobile policemen to respond. A local source said the attackers fled into nearby bushes when they sighted the advancing security personnel. According to the source, the security forces subsequently launched a follow-up operation to track the fleeing assailants and restore normalcy in the area. “During the operation, the troops reportedly recovered the body of a Police Inspector who was killed during the attack,” the source said. He added that the remains of the slain officer were deposited at the Ayilamo Hospital mortuary for autopsy and other necessary procedures. Confirming the incident, the Benue State Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, DSP Peter Aondongu, said the command lost one of its personnel in the attack. “I can confirm that we lost one of our officers in Ayilamo, as the report stated. Operations in that axis are still ongoing to bring the perpetrators to book,” Aondongu said. Meanwhile, security forces have intensified patrols and surveillance around Uzer, Ayilamo and other border communities in Logo LGA following the attack. items.title: Ofankor crash death toll rises to 12, 22 injured – NRSA confirms
items.description: The death toll from Thursday morning’s multi-vehicle crash along the John Teye-Ofankor corridor has risen to 12, the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has confirmed. The crash, which occurred on Thursday, August 13, 2026, involved seven vehicles, including two heavily loaded tipper trucks, two passenger Sprinter buses, two private saloon cars and a tricycle. Several other people sustained injuries and are receiving treatment at the Ga North Municipal Hospital and Achimota Hospital, according to the NRSA. The Authority expressed its condolences to the bereaved families and transport associations affected by the tragedy. “This painful incident is a reminder of the urgent need for greater responsibility and vigilance on our roads,” the NRSA said. The Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service, together with other stakeholders, is assisting with traffic management and efforts to restore normal movement along the affected corridor. The NRSA said it was concerned about the rising number of fatal crashes across the country and was intensifying public education and enforcement measures to address the trend. It reminded motorists of the statutory speed limits of 90km/h on highways, 50km/h in urban settlements and 30km/h in built-up areas . The Authority also urged vehicle owners and operators to ensure their vehicles are roadworthy before embarking on journeys. It noted that mechanical failures, particularly when combined with excessive speeding, can contribute significantly to road crashes. “Regular maintenance checks are essential to prevent avoidable tragedies,” the statement said. The NRSA said it would continue working with transport unions, civil society organisations and the Ghana Police Service to strengthen road safety interventions. “Road safety is a shared responsibility,” the Authority stressed. It described the Ofankor-Barrier crash as a painful reminder of the consequences of negligence and non-compliance with road safety regulations. “As the nation mourns the lives lost, the NRSA reaffirms its dedication to protecting every Ghanaian on the road,” it added.

items.title: FG, BOA partner to lift 80m vulnerable Nigerians out of poverty
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has partnered with the Bank of Agriculture, BOA, to transition millions of vulnerable Nigerians from dependence on humanitarian assistance to sustainable livelihoods through access to agricultural finance, productive assets, skills and enterprise opportunities. The partnership was formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, between the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction and the BOA. The initiative is designed to link beneficiaries of government’s social protection programmes with agricultural financing, inputs, value-chain opportunities and other interventions aimed at increasing their productivity and incomes. Speaking at the signing of the agreement, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro, said the National Social Register contains information on about 20 million vulnerable households, representing approximately 80 million individuals. Doro described the database as the largest of its kind in Africa, adding that more than 10 million individuals captured in the register had so far been validated with their National Identification Numbers, NIN. He said the database would provide government and development partners with a credible platform to identify beneficiaries and tailor interventions to their specific needs rather than relying on blanket programmes. “We have something to bring to this partnership, and you too have something definitely to bring,” Doro said, emphasising the complementary roles of the ministry and the BOA. The minister explained that inclusion in the National Social Register followed a process involving vulnerability assessments, community-based targeting, data collection, verification and analysis. He said community participation was essential because poverty manifests differently across regions and communities, making local knowledge important in identifying vulnerable households. Doro added that the subsequent validation of beneficiaries through NIN further strengthened the credibility of the register by ensuring that those captured were real and identifiable individuals. According to him, the Federal Government is now seeking to use the verified data to connect vulnerable Nigerians with opportunities that can improve their economic circumstances. He said the partnership was also part of the ministry’s broader reforms aimed at reducing duplication, wastage and leakages in humanitarian interventions while ensuring that government resources deliver measurable results. Doro said the ministry’s One Humanitarian, One Poverty Response System, OHOPRS, was designed to promote a coordinated approach to humanitarian response and poverty reduction. He explained that the collaboration with BOA would help translate the reforms into practical economic opportunities by connecting verified vulnerable Nigerians with agricultural finance, productive inputs, enterprise development and livelihood restoration programmes. Under the agreement, the two institutions will collaborate in areas including poverty reduction, agricultural financing, humanitarian interventions, social investment, financial inclusion, women’s economic empowerment, youth development, climate resilience, skills acquisition, rural development, food security, digital financial services, value-chain development and enterprise development. The initiative is expected to bridge the gap between social protection and economic empowerment by helping vulnerable households transition gradually from short-term assistance to productive economic activities. The Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of BOA, Ayodeji Oludare, said the bank was prepared to provide the financial and technical support required to improve the productivity and earning capacity of beneficiaries. He said the support could include agricultural inputs such as fertiliser and seeds, as well as financing and other interventions designed to increase productivity. Oludare disclosed that the bank could also develop economic profiles for participating farmers to enable it understand their activities and establish appropriate credit-scoring mechanisms that would improve access to finance. He stressed that BOA’s commitment would extend beyond a single intervention, noting that the bank would continue to explore additional funding opportunities and expand the partnership to make it a sustainable solution for vulnerable Nigerians. Under the MoU, the ministry will facilitate access to eligible beneficiaries, coordinate relevant humanitarian and social protection programmes, engage government institutions and other stakeholders, provide policy guidance and support implementation. BOA, on its part, will develop financing interventions, agricultural financing solutions, financial inclusion initiatives, value-chain financing and financial products tailored to the needs of vulnerable groups. The bank will also provide financial advisory and technical expertise and participate, where appropriate, in programme implementation, monitoring and evaluation. The partnership is also expected to replace the traditional one-size-fits-all approach to social intervention with a data-driven beneficiary profiling system. Through the system, beneficiaries can be assessed based on their economic activities, circumstances and specific needs, enabling financing, inputs and livelihood interventions to be matched more accurately with those who require them. The agreement could also facilitate the mobilisation of additional resources from development partners, donor agencies, private-sector organisations and multilateral institutions to scale successful programmes. The post FG, BOA partner to lift 80m vulnerable Nigerians out of poverty appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Sissili/Solidarité : Le Groupe Sanfo offre du matériel d’une valeur d’un million de F CFA à plusieurs structures locales Léo, 12 août 2026 (AIB) — Le Groupe Sanfo a fait parler son cœur, ce mercredi 12 août 2026 à Léo, en faisant don d’un lot de matériel d’une valeur totale d’un million de francs CFA au profit des Volontaires Adjoints de sécurité (VADS), des services provinciaux, des communes et de la communauté musulmane. La cérémonie de remise officielle, présidée par le haut-commissaire de la province, Téwindé Isaac Sia, s’est déroulée dans une atmosphère de reconnaissance mutuelle. Ce don est composé de 30 fûts, 4 foyers, 15 tenues pour les VADS, 100 bouilloires ainsi que de tables en bois, destinés à renforcer l’équipement et les conditions de travail des structures bénéficiaires. S’exprimant lors de la cérémonie, le haut-commissaire de la province, Téwindé Isaac Sia, a témoigné la reconnaissance des autorités provinciales. « C’est avec une grande joie que je reçois ce don, et je tiens à remercier chaleureusement le donateur pour cette belle initiative », a-t-il déclaré. Le chef de l’exécutif provincial a en outre souligné qu’il ne s’agissait pas d’une première pour le généreux donateur. « Comme vous le savez, ce n’est pas la première fois qu’un tel geste est posé : c’est déjà la troisième fois que nous en bénéficions. Nous nous rappelons notamment des actions menées en 2024 dans le domaine de la sécurité. Ce que je souhaite exprimer aujourd’hui, c’est véritablement toute notre gratitude. » Pour le donateur, Mohamed Sanfo, PDG du Groupe Sanfo, une entreprise spécialisée dans le commerce du bois et des matériaux de construction, ce geste s’inscrit dans le cadre du devoir civique et du patriotisme. « Je suis très content de pouvoir faire ce don parce que je trouve que c’est un devoir pour nous citoyens de soutenir l’administration afin qu’elle nous offre de meilleurs services. C’est également pour répondre à l’appel du Président du Faso à l’engagement citoyen pour le développement de notre pays. C’est pourquoi depuis 2022, je me suis engagé à faire ce que je peux pour soutenir là où le besoin se fait sentir », a expliqué le chef d’entreprise. Du côté des bénéficiaires, la satisfaction est tout aussi vive. S’exprimant au nom de l’ensemble des structures destinataires, le représentant des VADS a témoigné sa profonde gratitude envers les acteurs de cette chaîne de solidarité : « Je suis sincèrement ému par ce geste à notre endroit et je ne peux que remercier le donateur qui a eu cette idée à notre égard. Au nom de mes collègues et moi-même, je dis également merci aux autorités et à notre hiérarchie qui nous encouragent chaque jour. Une fois de plus, je réitère mes remerciements à tous. » Ce geste citoyen vient une fois de plus réaffirmer la mobilisation des acteurs économiques locaux aux côtés de l’administration et des acteurs de terrain. items.title: Corruption: ICPC urges Nigerians to reject ‘everyone is doing it’ mindset
items.description: By Progress Godfrey ABUJA – The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has urged Nigerians to reject the perception that corruption is inevitable and “everyone is doing it”, warning that such narratives could weaken resistance to corrupt practices. Chairman of ICPC, Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, said messages that focus only on how widespread corruption is could breed fatigue, resignation and, in some cases, normalise the conduct they seek to condemn. Aliyu stressed that anti-corruption communication should instead highlight positive social norms and show citizens that the majority reject corruption, while linking the message to tangible outcomes such as completed projects, recovered funds and improved public services. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday while delivering a keynote address at the 4th Economic Confidential Lecture and 6th National Spokespersons Awards, organised by Image Merchants Promotion Limited, publishers of Economic Confidential, on the theme, “Anti-Corruption Reforms, Economic Stability and Effective Communication.” The ICPC Chief also said the rising rate of citizen reporting of corruption indicated that Nigerians were increasingly willing to resist corrupt practices, adding that public institutions must communicate honestly, consistently and proactively. According to him, “The evidence, however, cautions us that communication must be strategic, not merely loud. Emerging research on anti-corruption communication, including guidance from the Basel Institute on Governance, suggests that messages which simply emphasise how widespread corruption is can inadvertently backfire, breeding fatigue and resignation rather than action, and in some cases even normalising the very conduct they seek to condemn. “This is because such messages tend to confirm the belief that corruption is inevitable and that ‘everyone is doing it,’ thereby weakening the individual’s resolve to resist it.” Aliyu further said the media has a strategic role in the anti-corruption campaign, but stressed that credibility remains its greatest asset, with accuracy, professionalism, fairness and objectivity taking precedence over sensationalism. Earlier in his remarks, the Publisher of Economic Confidential, Yushau A. Shuaib, said the 2026 lecture was designed to examine the relationship between anti-corruption reforms, economic stability and strategic communication, particularly their role in strengthening public trust and institutional credibility. Shuaib noted that the National Spokespersons Awards, formally launched in 2020, had continued to recognise professionalism, excellence and integrity in public communication, while the organisation also unveiled its research project on Artificial Intelligence in Crisis Communication in Nigeria. He added that the research, reviewed by communication scholars, was supported by the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and shortlisted for the 2026 Golden World Awards in Athens, Greece. items.title: Flood: Nasarawa to redesign drainages, waterways in Lafia
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia LAFIA — The Nasarawa State Government has commenced plans to redesign drainage systems and waterways in Lafia, the state capital, following flooding that damaged buildings, disrupted transportation and displaced residents on Thursday. The Managing Director of the Nasarawa State Urban Development Board (NUDB), Engr. Muhammad Yahaya Wada, disclosed this while speaking with journalists in his office in Lafia. Wada said he had briefed Governor Abdullahi Sule on the extent of the flooding and had received approval to review the existing designs of drainage channels and waterways in the affected areas. He said the review became necessary after the flooding exposed gaps in the initial designs and affected areas that were not adequately captured. “I have already briefed the governor, though he is out of town, and he has given us the go-ahead initially to check the situation. I briefed him on our findings, and he has given us the go-ahead to update our design so that we will start,” Wada said. “We have seen the damage, and it gives us the opportunity to update our design and improve on it because, from what happened today, we noticed that there are other places that were not captured in our initial design.” The NUDB boss said the immediate priority was to assess the affected areas and improve the drainage and water-channel designs, noting that a complete reconstruction of new channels might not be possible during the current rainy season. He, however, advised residents living along waterways and flood-prone areas to relocate temporarily to safer locations, warning that further rainfall could worsen the situation. “We will advise people along that area to stay away, to keep off and vacate the places for now because you wouldn’t know when it will come again or how heavier it will be. “It could be heavier than what we experienced, and it could happen at night. So, we will advise people to stay away and vacate where they are living for now, until maybe after the season,” he said. Wada said the flooding affected several areas, including Millionaire Quarters and Bukan Sidi, while some roads, including federal highways, were cut off. He said officials of the board had visited the affected areas to assess the extent of the damage and interact with residents. According to him, the condition of some buildings had become a source of concern, with cracks appearing on some structures and others collapsing. He said the government did not currently have the mandate to forcibly remove residents from flood-prone areas but would continue to sensitise them on the dangers of remaining in such locations. “As regards forcing people to leave the place, I think we don’t have that mandate. We only advise and sensitise them on the implications of living there,” he said. Wada said the structural integrity of some buildings could no longer be guaranteed, citing collapsed toilets, soakaways and concrete wells as evidence of possible damage to their foundations. “Where we checked, we have seen that the integrity of most of the buildings cannot be vouched for. Some toilets have already collapsed, some soakaways collapsed, some concrete wells have already collapsed. That tells you that the substructure is weak, and some houses are completely flooded,” he said. The NUDB managing director warned that any building located within the right-of-way of drainage channels would have to give way if the government embarked on reconstruction. He said such action would be taken in the overall public interest, in accordance with the relevant regulations. Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Dr. Margaret Elayo, who inspected areas affected by the flooding, ordered the temporary closure of Sandaji Hotel. The government urged residents in affected areas to remain vigilant, avoid waterways and other flood-prone locations, and cooperate with authorities as measures are taken to address the immediate risks and redesign the drainage system. items.title: Orpaillage artisanal : le Dr Ahmed Koama plaide pour une protection renforcée des enfants contre le paludisme
items.description: BURKINA-SANTÉ-ORPAILLAGE-PALUDISME-ENFANTS Orpaillage artisanal : le Dr Ahmed Koama plaide pour une protection renforcée des enfants contre le paludisme Ouagadougou, 12 août 2026 (AIB)-Le Dr Ahmed Koama, président de l'Association Wend La Laafi et spécialiste en ophtalmologie et en santé-sécurité-environnement, a formulé une série de recommandations destinées à mieux protéger les enfants du paludisme sur les sites d'orpaillage artisanal du Burkina Faso, dans une analyse rendue publique récemment. Ahmed Koama, les milliers d'enfants présents sur ces sites sont exposés à de multiples risques sanitaires : poussière de silice, mercure, accidents et eaux stagnantes propices à la prolifération des moustiques. Il relève que le paludisme, aggravé par la promiscuité et l'insalubrité qui caractérisent ces lieux, frappe particulièrement les plus jeunes, dont les parents, contraints par la survie économique, travaillent souvent à leurs côtés malgré les dangers. « Sur un site minier artisanal, protéger un enfant du paludisme est une responsabilité collective », affirme le Dr Koama, qui appelle parents, exploitants, responsables de sites, leaders communautaires et agents de santé à se mobiliser conjointement. Pour une protection efficace, l'expert recommande cinq actions prioritaires : faire dormir chaque enfant sous une moustiquaire imprégnée d'insecticide chaque nuit, limiter les piqûres de moustiques en soirée par le port de vêtements couvrants, et améliorer l'environnement des lieux de vie en évitant les eaux stagnantes et en sécurisant les excavations abandonnées. Il préconise également l'administration de la chimioprophylaxie antipaludique selon les directives nationales et sous supervision médicale. Enfin, il insiste sur la nécessité de consulter rapidement un service de santé devant toute fièvre chez un enfant, le paludisme pouvant évoluer rapidement chez les plus jeunes. Le Dr Ahmed Koama est un spécialiste reconnu des questions de santé en milieu minier artisanal. Il a soutenu, le 25 juillet 2025 à l'Institut national des sciences appliquées (INSA) de Bobo-Dioulasso, une thèse de doctorat en santé, sécurité et environnement consacrée aux risques sanitaires sur les sites d'orpaillage, sanctionnée par la mention très honorable avec félicitations du jury. En tant que président de l'Association Wend La Laafi, il a par ailleurs conduit, en septembre 2025 à Ouagadougou, une campagne de consultations gratuites en santé oculaire, visant à sensibiliser les populations à l'importance du dépistage précoce des pathologies des yeux. Agence d'information du Burkina RK/ata

items.title: Boulgou : L’ONI rapproche la délivrance de la CIB-AES des populations de Niaogho
items.description: Boulgou : L'ONI rapproche la délivrance de la CIB-AES des populations de Niaogho Niaogho, 08 août 2026 -AIB- Dans le cadre de sa politique de proximité visant à rapprocher les services de l'Office national d'identification -ONI- des populations, une équipe de l'antenne régionale de l'ONI du Nakambé a effectué, ce samedi, une sortie dans la commune de Niaogho, province du Boulgou. Conduite par l'adjudant-chef de police Sami Fausien Poda, du Centre de traitement informatique des données -CTID- du Boulgou, l'équipe a d'abord été reçue par le secrétaire général de la mairie, Ambroise Bayili, représentant le président de la délégation spéciale. Elle s'est ensuite rendue à la cour royale de Niaogho où elle a présenté aux notables du palais du chef de canton et aux autorités communales, le nouvel agent collecteur communal, Dieudonné Ouédraogo, de la brigade de gendarmerie de Niaogho. A cette occasion, les autorités coutumières et communales ont pu bénéficier de l'opération d'enrôlement pour l'établissement de la nouvelle carte d'identité burkinabè de l'AES, la CIB-AES. Cette démarche s'inscrit dans la dynamique de déconcentration des services de l'ONI et marque une étape importante dans la prise en compte progressive de la commune de Niaogho dans le dispositif de collecte de la CIB-AES. Au nom de l'autorité coutumière, le représentant du chef de canton, Gaisdouma Compaoré, a salué cette innovation très attendue par les populations. « Nous sommes ravis de cette avancée décisive et nous témoignons notre profonde reconnaissance aux responsables de la commune ainsi qu'au ministre de la Sécurité qui a bien voulu prêter une oreille attentive à notre cri de cœur », a-t-il déclaré. Le président de la cérémonie, Ambroise Bayili, a souligné la portée pratique de cette déconcentration. Désormais, l'ensemble de la procédure d'enrôlement sera assuré sur place, à la brigade de gendarmerie de Niaogho, par l'agent Dieudonné Ouédraogo, spécialement formé pour servir de point focal communal. « Cette concrétisation est le fruit d'un plaidoyer éclairé mené par Sa Majesté Naaba Wobgo II, chef de Niaogho, lors de la cérémonie de clôture des travaux du mur de clôture de la gendarmerie locale, auprès du ministre en charge de la Sécurité », a-t-il indiqué. Saluant la synergie d'actions sur le terrain, l'adjudant-chef Sami Fausien Poda a exprimé sa gratitude aux responsables communaux ainsi qu'aux chefs coutumiers et religieux, dont la franche collaboration et l'engagement patriotique ont été déterminants pour le succès de ce déploiement opérationnel. C'est dans une atmosphère de convivialité et de fierté que la cérémonie a pris fin, marquant une étape symbolique dans l'affirmation de la citoyenneté au sein de l'espace AES. Agence d'Information du Burkina AA/SM/ata

items.title: Mali pardons Frenchman jailed 20 years over alleged coup plot
items.description: A Frenchman who was sentenced to 20 years in prison in Mali for plotting an alleged coup in the West African country has now been granted a presidential pardon, it was announced on Thursday. Yann Vezilier was accused a year ago of trying to destabilise President Assimi Goïta’s government “on behalf of the French intelligence service” alongside a number of army generals and dozens of soldiers. It is not yet clear what has prompted Mali’s U-turn. France’s foreign ministry has yet to comment on the pardon, and previously said accusations that Vezilier was working in Mali as a French spy were “unfounded”. In a post on Facebook, the Malian government said: “This act of clemency, which does not call into question the facts established by an adversarial judgment rendered during a trial, where all rights of the defence were respected, is accompanied by the immediate removal of the individual from national territory.” Mali is a former colony of France, and has been gripped by a security crisis fuelled by an Islamist insurgency since 2012. It was one of the reasons given for Goïta leading a coup in 2021, but attacks by jihadist groups have continued and even increased. At the time of the arrests last year, Mali’s Security Minister Gen Daoud Aly Mohammedine said “fringe elements of the Malian armed security forces” had been detained for seeking to “destabilise the institutions of the republic”. “These soldiers and civilians” were said to have obtained “the help of foreign states”, the minister said. Vezilier was said to have acted “on behalf of the French intelligence service, which mobilised political leaders, civil society actors and military personnel” in Mali, according to the minister. Political tension and the security crisis have worsened in Mali. In April the country’s defence minister was killed in an apparent suicide truck bombing on his residence near the capital, Bamako, during a wave of militant attacks. Goïta named himself defence minister shortly after, in an apparent attempt to consolidate his already considerable power. When the capital came under siege by Islamist fighters, they managed to impose a partial blockade there and total blockades elsewhere, including the city of Ségou. Last May, the junta dissolved all political parties following rare anti-government protests, which former Prime Minister Moussa Mara described as a severe blow to reconciliation efforts initiated by the military leaders. Goïta had promised elections within two years of seizing power, but these have never been held. Last July, the transition period was extended by five years, clearing him to continue leading the country until at least 2030.

items.title: Pakistan Army major general appointed new force commander of UN mission in Western Sahara
items.description: Pakistan Army Major General Jawwad Ahmed Qazi has been appointed the new force commander of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso), the Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the UN announced on Thursday. In a social media post on X, Pakistan’s mission said, “UN Secretary General António Guterres has appointed Major Gen Qazi of Pakistan as the new force commander of Minurso.” “With over 35 years of leadership and operational experience in the Pakistan Army and UN peacekeeping, Major Gen Qazi brings extensive command, field and international experience to the mission,” the mission said. According to Pakistan’s mission, Major Gen Qazi has previously served in senior leadership roles, including command, staff and instructional positions, both in Pakistan and abroad. His previous appointments in Pakistan include general officer commanding of an infantry division, force commander in the Northern Areas and director general at the Ministry of Defence, it added. Earlier in his career, he also served with the UN Transitional Administration for Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Sirmium (UNTAES) in Croatia. “Pakistan takes pride in this appointment and remains committed to supporting UN peacekeeping and international efforts for peace and stability through deployment of mission-ready contingents and leaders who have vast peacekeeping experience,” it stated. Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony largely controlled by Morocco, is the only territory on the African continent whose post-colonial status has not been settled. Morocco has long been in conflict with the Algerian-backed Polisario Front, which seeks independence for the Sahrawi people. It is claimed by the Polisario Front, which insists on the indigenous Sahrawi people’s right to a referendum on self-determination monitored by the UN. Polisario is seeking independence and says Morocco should adhere to an agreement it accepted in 1991 that provides for a UN-supervised referendum on self-determination.

items.title: One dead, six injured in blast at Rotterdam petroleum storage facility
items.description: A blast at a storage facility for petroleum products at the Netherlands’ ​Rotterdam port killed one person and wounded six others on Thursday, officials ‌said, as police investigated the cause of the explosion. A spokesperson for major energy commodities trading company Gunvor said an “incident” occurred during maintenance work on one of its storage tanks. A police spokesperson said ​that there was no immediate sign of sabotage and that all possible scenarios ​were under investigation. The port of Rotterdam is the largest in Europe ⁠and a major hub for crude oil and fuel imports and storage. It hosts ​Europe’s largest oil refinery, Shell’s 404,000-barrel-per-day Pernis plant, in addition to other oil refineries ​operated by BP, ExxonMobil and Vitol. The explosion occurred at around 11:30 a.m. (0930 GMT). Gunvor said it was cooperating with local authorities. Shell said its operations at the port were unaffected by the blast. A Rotterdam Port ​spokesperson said LNG terminals were not affected by the blast. Data from European gas transmission group ​ENTSOG showed a temporary drop in gas sendout from Rotterdam’s Gate LNG terminal, and then volatile ‌flows. ⁠It was not clear if that was a consequence of the blast or an unrelated power outage elsewhere in the sprawling port. Any prolonged disruption would be closely watched by traders, as Gate is one of northwest Europe’s key LNG import hubs and ​Dutch gas storage sites ​are currently only ⁠around 40% full, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe data, ahead of the winter heating season. ExxonMobil said the power outage had ​been resolved and that its operations were normal at its 191,000-barrel-per-day ​refinery, declining ⁠to confirm an alert from Wood Mackenzie seen by Reuters that all monitored units had shut down. Rotterdam Port said there was no connection between the blast and the power ⁠outage. The port ​had experienced several power outages earlier in the ​day, but none were connected to the blast, the local safety authority said.

Saluant le dévouement du corps professoral qui œuvre « nuit et jour pour façonner les futurs bâtisseurs de la nation », il a lancé un appel à la cohésion et à la rigueur. « Une collaboration franche et sincère entre enseignants, élèves, parents et direction est indispensable pour garantir la réussite collective. Un suivi rigoureux des apprenants, à la maison comme à l'école, est exigé pour enrayer la baisse des résultats scolaires. Aucune complaisance ne sera tolérée face au non-respect des règles de travail », a-t-il martelé. Prenant la parole avec émotion, la nouvelle directrice du CEG de Kièflè, Lamoussa Elisabeth Sam, a traduit sa reconnaissance à sa hiérarchie pour la confiance placée en elle et rendu un hommage appuyé à son prédécesseur. « J'accueille cette charge avec humilité et détermination », a-t-elle affirmé, tout en sollicitant l'accompagnement sincère de ses collaborateurs pour réussir sa mission de renouveau éducatif. items.title: Baby stolen at birth in Benue; Police nab 11 suspects
items.description: By Peter Duru, MAKURDI The Benue State Police Command has rescued a newborn baby allegedly stolen shortly after delivery at a healthcare facility in Gboko, arresting 11 suspects in connection with the incident. The baby, according to the Police, was rescued from the custody of the alleged principal suspect and subsequently reunited with the mother. The State Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, DSP Peter Aondongu, who disclosed this in a statement on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Cletus Nwadiogbu, said the incident was reported to the Command on August 12, 2026. He said, “On 12 August 2026, at about 11a.m., operatives of the Command attached to A Division, Gboko, received a complaint from one Aondofa Chia, whose wife delivered a baby shortly at a healthcare facility in Gboko, that the newborn baby had gone missing.” According to him, the police immediately commenced investigation following the report, leading to the arrest of nine suspects who were taken in for questioning and to assist investigators in unraveling the circumstances surrounding the disappearance.” Aondongu said further investigation resulted in the arrest of two additional suspects at about 10p.m. the same day, bringing the number of suspects in police custody to 11. He identified the alleged principal suspect as 35-year-old Asugh, from whose custody the stolen newborn was recovered. “The stolen newborn baby was subsequently rescued from her custody and safely reunited with the mother,” the PPRO stated. He added that investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the incident and determine the roles allegedly played by each of the suspects and their respective degrees of culpability. Commending the operatives for what he described as their swift response and professional handling of the incident, the Commissioner of Police assured residents of the state that the Command remained committed to protecting lives and property. The CP said the police would continue to respond decisively to reports of crime and threats to public safety, while urging members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities. The Command also appealed to residents with credible information on criminal activities to report to the nearest police station or contact its emergency lines on 08066006475 and 07067374913. items.title: AfroBasket U18 : le Sénégal écarte Madagascar et rejoint le dernier carré
items.description: Le Sénégal continue son parcours en Afrobasket U18 masculin. Face à Madagascar, les jeunes Lions se sont imposés 54 à 40 ce jeudi 13 aout en quart de finale, validant ainsi leur place en demi-finale de la compétition. Dès l’entame, les Sénégalais démarrent fort en s'adjugeant le premier quart-temps 15-9, avant de connaître un passage à vide au deuxième acte, où Madagascar reprend la main (12-8) et ne compte plus que deux points de retard à la pause (23-21). Le tournant du match intervient au retour des vestiaires : le Sénégal hausse le ton défensivement et inflige un sévère 18-4 à ses adversaires sur le troisième quart-temps, un écart qui scelle pratiquement l'issue de la rencontre. À noter que ce succès repose largement sur la solidité défensive sénégalaise : 10 ballons interceptés, 5 contres, et 14 points inscrits en contre-attaque, autant d'éléments qui ont étouffé l'attaque malgache tout au long du match. Individuellement, Code Mbengue s'est distingué par sa constance et son impact sur l'ensemble de la rencontre, contribuant fortement à la qualification de son équipe. Après une deuxième place dans la poule C (deux victoires, une défaite), le Sénégal confirme ses ambitions dans cette édition 2026 de l'AfroBasket U18. Direction la demi-finale, où les jeunes Lions affronteront le Mali. O.B.N

items.title: Rescue operation underway as passenger train derails in southern England
items.description: UK police and emergency services are on scene after a passenger train derailed in southern England, authorities said Thursday. The incident happened around 3:54 p.m. (10:54 a.m. ET) near Lewes railway station in East Sussex, around 45 miles south of London, according to British Transport Police. “We’re responding alongside paramedics and the fire service and will provide more information as soon as we can,” BTP said on X. Images posted to social media appear to show several train carriages on their sides, with people standing on top of them. There are “no serious injuries or fatalities,” according to multiple British news outlets citing a source from the UK Department for Transport. East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service said it was working with other emergency services at the scene and advised the public to avoid the area. “We have ten fire engines, a Command Support Unit, technical rescue units, officers and other resources at the scene,” the fire service said in an update on Thursday evening. “We have been helping reach passengers and assisting other emergency services.” UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said she was “deeply concerned” by reports of the derailment and thanked emergency responders working at the scene to support those impacted. “We are working quickly with the rail industry and local partners to assist passengers,” she added. There was no immediate indication of the cause of the derailment. Some train services had been canceled and others were running at reduced speeds due to a heatwave – temperatures in some parts of southern England reached 35 degrees Celsius, or 95 degrees Fahrenheit on Thursday. The UK’s Rail Accident Investigation Branch said it was deploying a team of investigators to the site of the derailment to begin gathering evidence. Images circulating on social platforms shortly after the derailment showed overturned train carriages and emergency responders on scene. Laura Arnold The TSSA transport union also expressed its concern over the derailment. “With a large number of passengers involved, their safety and wellbeing must come first. We thank all emergency services and rail staff responding at the scene and await to hear more,” it said in a statement. Rail customers have been warned of “major disruption” for the next several hours, according to National Rail. “No trains can run through Lewes and Haywards Heath until further notice. You will need to use an alternative route to reach your destination,” it said. Train operator Southern Rail has advised the public not to travel with all lines through Lewes railway station shut down to allow emergency team, rail engineers and other specialist staff “to assess the situation and ensure the railway is safe.” Thursday’s incident is the second serious train crash in the UK in two months. In June, two passenger trains collided in south-central England near the town of Bedford, killing one person and injuring dozens more.

items.title: Incendies en Algérie : l’indemnisation des sinistrés lancée le 18 août
items.description: Le processus d’indemnisation des victimes des incendies qui ont frappé l’Algérie durant le mois de juillet est entré dans sa phase finale avec l’achèvement de l’opération d’évaluation des dégâts lancée par les autorités. L’annonce a été faite ce jeudi 13 août par le ministère de l’Intérieur et des Transports dans un communiqué. Le ministère de l'Intérieur, des collectivités locales et des Transports porte à la connaissance des citoyennes et des citoyens touchés par les incendies de forêts survenus durant le mois de juillet dernier, qu'en « exécution des instructions » du président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, visant la « prise en charge des dégâts occasionnés aux produits agricoles, aux habitations et aux mobiliers, équipements et appareils électroménagers, les travaux des commissions d'évaluation locales et celle nationale ont été clôturés mardi 11 août ». Incendies en Algérie : l’indemnisation des victimes à partir du 18 août Le département de Saïd Sayoud a ajouté que les listes des citoyennes et citoyens touchés et celle des dégâts éligibles à l'aide de l'État ont été « transmises aux secteurs et aux walis concernés pour exécution des décisions arrêtées ». Le ministère de l’Intérieur a indiqué que les citoyens concernés sont invités à « se rapprocher, à partir du mercredi 18 août, de leur communes de résidence, pour retirer leurs décisions d'octroi de l'aide de l'État. » L’Algérie a été touchée par une vague d’incendies inédite du 8 au 22 juillet durant laquelle six personnes ont perdu la vie. Les flammes ont ravagé des forêts et des récoltes, et endommagé des habitations dans certaines wilayas, comme Annaba et Bejaïa. L’article Incendies en Algérie : l’indemnisation des sinistrés lancée le 18 août est apparu en premier sur TSA .
